cards.text: Jesus has set out for Jerusalem (Luke 9:51), and here Luke calls Him the Lord. Now He appoints seventy-two others and sends them ahead of Him to every town and place He's about to visit. SEVENTY-TWO, friend, and I can't even get a dozen cookies out of the oven without dropping one.

cards.question: Jesus sends the seventy-two out one at a time, each one on his own.

cards.text: Before they go, Jesus gives them a picture: ‘The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.’ Big job, short staff, and every adult with a job just nodded.

cards.question: With a big harvest and only a few workers, what does Jesus tell the seventy-two to do?

answers.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers
Hire more workers from the towns nearby
Let the field rest until next season

cards.text: Then Jesus says, ‘Go!’ And He's honest about what's waiting out there, friend, no fine print on this box.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two He is sending them out like wolves among lambs.

cards.text: Jesus tells them what to leave behind, and then adds one more thing: do not greet anyone along the road. Friend, I greet every baker at my door like I haven't seen them in ten years, so that one would be HARD for me.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the seventy-two not to carry?

answers.text: A purse or bag or sandals
A staff or cloak or tunic
A lamp or scroll or blanket

cards.text: Whatever house they walk into, Jesus tells them to begin with these words: ‘Peace to this house.’ Not ‘Hey,’ not ‘Nice place,’ but PEACE.

cards.question: The seventy-two say ‘Peace to this house.’ If no man of peace is there, what happens to that peace?

answers.text: It stays on the house anyway

cards.text: Once they're welcomed into a house, Jesus says eat and drink whatever they're offered, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Whatever's on the table, you eat it, and friend, nobody has EVER had to tell me that twice when there's a warm cookie on it.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two to move to a new house every night so no one family carries the load.
When a town welcomes the seventy-two, they eat whatever is set before them. What else does Jesus send them to do there?

answers.text: Heal the sick and tell them God's kingdom is near
Teach the law and settle all their disputes
Gather the people and collect an offering

cards.text: But if a town doesn't welcome them, they go into the streets and declare, ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you.’ Friend, I spent years under junk drawer dust, and nobody EVER wiped me off that dramatically.

cards.question: Even to a town that won't welcome them, the seventy-two still declare, ‘Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is ___.’

cards.text: Jesus says that on that day, it will be more bearable for Sodom than for that town. Then He calls out two towns by name: ‘Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!’

cards.question: Jesus says if the miracles performed in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, those cities would have ___ long ago.

cards.text: Jesus says it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for those towns. Then He calls out one more: ‘And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven?’

cards.question: Jesus tells Capernaum it will be lifted up to heaven.
Jesus tells the seventy-two that whoever listens to them listens to Him, and whoever rejects them rejects Him. Who else does that person reject?

cards.text: Mission over, and the seventy-two come back to Jesus with a report. Friend, if those were my bakers, I'd be pacing by the door with my mustache in a knot waiting to hear how it went.

cards.question: What do the seventy-two tell Jesus when they get back?

answers.text: Even the demons submit to them in His name
The dead were raised in every town
Fire fell from heaven at their word

cards.question: The seventy-two come back from their trip discouraged and worn out.

cards.text: Jesus answers them, ‘I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.’ That's Satan, the devil, and one sentence from Jesus about him hits like thunder.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two He has given them authority over all the power of the enemy.

cards.text: Jesus tells them He has given them authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and nothing will harm them. Then He says, ‘Nevertheless,’ and friend, when somebody says nevertheless, the whole conversation is about to turn around.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two not to rejoice that the spirits submit to them. What should they rejoice about instead?

answers.text: That their names are written in heaven
That every town will remember them
That they will see greater miracles

cards.text: At that time Jesus rejoices in the Holy Spirit and declares, ‘I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth.’ Friend, when the Son of God is THIS full of joy, you lean in and you listen.

cards.question: Jesus praises the Father for hiding these things from the wise and learned and revealing them to ___.
Jesus says all things have been entrusted to Him by His Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the ___.

cards.text: And it goes the other way too: no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him. That's not something you crack on your own, friend.
Then Jesus turns to the disciples and says privately, ‘Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.’ Just them, friend, a FRONT-ROW seat.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that many people wanted to see what they see and hear what they hear, but never did. Who?
